headline: In all three filings the reported top line rests on a component moving well out of proportion to its weight, and in each case the risk-factor language was rewritten in the same period that component moved.

lines.note: Revenue moved -2.9% while operating income fell 38% and interest income supplied 32% of pre-tax income; automotive regulatory credits at 2.8% of revenue carried 26.9% of the top-line change, and two closed 2024 quarters had their net income revised after the fact (Class A).

Reported revenue of $81.61B for the quarter ended 2026-04-26 is the highest of 63 reported periods, but two of three tested 'record' statements hold only within the same fiscal quarter, networking carried 21.5% of the annual change at 10.0% of the base, and R&D fell to 8.6% of revenues from 9.9% (Class A, with the release Class B).

Software and services at 9.6% of revenue carried 257.8% of the revenue movement while new electric vehicles fell $522.00M and regulatory credits fell $136.00M; in the same filing the competition risk factor was rewritten to cover software and services markets and the tariff factor moved from 'could be' to 'has been' affected (Class A).

gaps: Management claims were largely untestable across the set: 8 of 10 for Tesla, 7 of 10 for NVIDIA, 9 of 10 for Rivian could not be matched to a filed figure.

Where a check crossed no threshold it supplies no figures — NVIDIA and Rivian financial condition, Rivian restatements, NVIDIA single-source supply language — so those areas cannot be characterized at all from this material.
Revenue composition for all three was read from annual disaggregation or segment schedules only; no interim period composition was checked for any of them.

NHTSA coverage for Tesla and Rivian is scoped to model years 2024-2026 and to US campaigns; the Class F reports of a Tesla recall of nearly 3 million vehicles in China have no Class A counterpart here. NVIDIA's safety check does not apply rather than being a gap.

No news or community material was collected for Rivian at all, so its filings have nothing outside them to be set against; Tesla and NVIDIA have Class F press only, which corroborates but establishes nothing.
Per-share figures are excluded from the restatement check for all three registrants.
NVIDIA's tested release quotes two different first-quarter revenue figures, $81.6 billion and $75.2 billion, and the material does not reconcile them.
Several risk factor excerpts are truncated mid-sentence for Tesla and Rivian, so the full text of some added and removed factors could not be read.
